The Children of Israel said to Musa: "You killed him; he was more beloved to us than you and gentler." So they harmed him because of that. Allah commanded the angels, upon them be peace, to carry him, and they passed by him over the gatherings of the Children of Israel, and the angels, upon them be peace, spoke of his death. Thus Allah cleared him, and they went off with him and buried him, and no one knew his grave except the vulture (rakham). Allah made him deaf and mute.

In another narration from Ibn Abbas and some of the Companions: Allah revealed to Musa, "I am causing Harun to die, so go to such-and-such a mountain." So the two of them set out toward the mountain, and there he found a tree and a house in which was a couch with bedding and a pleasant fragrance. When Harun saw that mountain, the house and what was in it, he was delighted and said: "O Musa, I wish to sleep on this couch." He said: "Sleep on it." He said: "Sleep with me." So when they both slept, death seized Harun. When he was taken, that house was lifted, the tree disappeared, and the couch was raised to heaven. When Musa returned to the Children of Israel, they said: "He killed Harun, and envied him because of the Children of Israel's love for him. Harun was gentler and softer toward them, while there was some harshness in Musa toward them." When this reached him, he said: "Woe to you! He was my brother; do you think I would kill him?" When they pressed him, he stood, prayed two rak'ahs, then supplicated Allah, and the couch descended until they saw it between heaven and earth, and they believed him.

It is also said: what they attributed to him, upon him be peace, was fornication, and far be it from him. It is narrated that Qarun incited a prostitute to accuse him, upon him be peace, with herself, and gave her a great amount of wealth. She confessed to the bargain between her and Qarun, and what was done to him was done, as detailed in surah al-Qasas. This view is extremely remote, as the relative pronoun has been gathered (in the verse).

It is also said: what they attributed to him was sorcery and madness. It is also said: it is what was related of them in the Qur'an, of their saying: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight; we are sitting right here﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 24], ﴿We will never endure one kind of food﴾ [al-Baqarah: 61], and their saying: ﴿We will never believe you until we see Allah openly﴾ [al-Baqarah: 55], and other such things. It is possible to take what they said as including all of what has been mentioned.

﴿And he was honored (wajih) in the sight of Allah﴾. That is, he was one of high standing and rank with Him, mighty and majestic. Similar in meaning is the saying of Qutrub: he was of high rank. Similar to it is the saying of Ibn Zayd: he was accepted. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Hasan that he said: "Wajih" means one whose supplications are answered. Some added: he never asked for anything without being given it, except seeing Allah in this world. It is not hidden that the answering of supplications is among the branches of elevated rank. It is also said: his honor, upon him be peace, was that Allah spoke to him, and he was given the title "Kalim Allah" (the one spoken to by Allah).

Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash and Abu Haywah read ("'abdan") from servitude (al-'ubudiyyah), with ("li-Llah") with the genitive particle, so that ("'abdan") is the predicate of kana and ("wajihan") is an attribute of it. This is an irregular reading (qira'ah shadhdhah), and there is discussion about the validity of irregular readings.

Ibn Khalawayh said: "I prayed behind Ibn Shanbudh in the month of Ramadan, and I heard him reading ('abdan li-Llah') according to the reading of Ibn Mas'ud." Perhaps Ibn Shanbudh was among those who hold that recitation with it is valid without qualification, and something similar may be assumed of Ibn Khalawayh; otherwise al-Tibi said: the author of al-Rawdah said: "An irregular reading is valid if it contains no change of meaning, no addition of a letter, and no omission." Here there is a clear difference between the two meanings, as al-Zamakhshari's words indicate, and similarly from Ibn Jinni.

O you who have believed, fear Allah. (This applies) in all that you do and refrain from, especially in committing what Allah dislikes, let alone what hurts His Messenger and beloved (ﷺ). ﴿And speak﴾ in every matter of affairs ﴿words of appropriate justice﴾: intending and aiming at the target of truth. It derives from سَدَّ يَسِدُّ, with a kasra on the sin, سِدادًا, and with a fatha on it, سَدَادًا. One says سَدَّدَ سَهْمَهُ (saddada sahmahu, "he aimed his arrow"), when he directs it toward the intended mark and does not deviate it from its aim. The intended meaning, as has been said, is a prohibition against the opposite of this speech, which is speech that is not سَدِيدٌ (sadid, "upright"). This includes what was said in the matter of Zaynab of unjust speech that deviates from justice and uprightness, and likewise every speech that hurts him, upon him be prayers and peace. It is also reported from Muqatil and Qatadah that the meaning is: "And speak a sadid word concerning the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace, and Zayd and Zaynab." It is reported from Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah that the sadid speech is specifically لا إلَهَ إلّا اللَّهُ (la ilaha illa Allah, "there is no god but Allah"). It has also been said that it is what its outward form agrees with its inward reality. It has been said too that it is what contains reform. Perhaps what we have indicated is the most preferable.

﴿He will set right for you your deeds﴾ by accepting them and rewarding them, as is related from Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil. It was also said that the setting right of deeds is the granting of success in bringing them about in a righteous and pleasing manner.

﴿And He will forgive you your sins﴾ and make them expiated by your uprightness in speech and knowledge. ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾ in the commands and prohibitions, among which are those contained in these verses, ﴿has indeed achieved a great success﴾ in both abodes, ﴿a tremendous success﴾ whose measure cannot be estimated and whose limit cannot be reached.

Al-Kashshaf says: This verse, meaning ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah...﴾ to its end, confirms the one before it. That one was built on the prohibition of what harms the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this one on the command to fear Allah in guarding the tongue, so that prohibition and command follow one another. The prohibition is followed by what contains the threat from the story of Musa (peace be upon him), because describing him with his high standing with Allah the Exalted implies that Allah avenged him against the one who harmed him. The command is followed by the eloquent promise, so that the restraint from harm and the motivation to abandon it grow stronger. End of quotation. So do not be heedless.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 33, verse 72:

﴿Indeed, We offered the trust (al-amanah) to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it.﴾ When the Exalted One clarified the great status of obedience to God the Exalted and His Messenger (ﷺ), by showing the fate of those who depart from it, namely a painful punishment, and the attainment of those who observe it, namely a great triumph, He followed this with the great status of the legal obligations (al-takalif al-shar'iyyah) that necessitate it and the difficulty of its matter, by way of illustration (bi-tariq al-tamthil). This comes together with the indication that what proceeds from them of obedience and its abandonment proceeds from them after acceptance and commitment, without any compulsion or predetermination there.

He expressed it as "trust" (amanah), which in origin is a verbal noun like amn and aman, to draw attention to the fact that these are rights to be safeguarded, which God the Exalted deposited with the responsible persons (al-mukallafin) and entrusted them with, and obligated them to receive them with good obedience and submission, and commanded them to observe them, guard them, and discharge them without neglecting any of their rights. He expressed the importance of it, in relation to the readiness of what was mentioned of the heavens and others with regard to particularities, by "offering" it to them, to show exceeding care for its matter and the desire for them to accept it. And [he expressed] their lack of readiness to accept it, and its incompatibility with what they are upon, by "declining" and "fearing" it, to magnify its matter and to nurture its grandeur. And [he expressed] their acceptance of it by "bearing" (al-haml), to realize the meaning of the difficulty considered in it by making it of the kind of heavy bodies. The meaning is that this trust is of such great importance that, if those great bodies, which are a proverb for strength and vigor, were charged with observing it, and were possessed of perception and awareness, they would have declined to accept it and feared it. But the speech is turned away from its usual course, by depicting the supposed as if it were realized, for the sake of greater confirmation of the intended meaning and its clarification.

﴿And man bore it﴾, i.e., this species (hadha al-jins), like: ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful to his Lord﴾ [al-Adiyat: 6] and ﴿Indeed, man transgresses﴾ [al-Alaq: 6]. His bearing of it is either by considering it in relation to his readiness, or by his being charged with it on the Day of Covenant (yawm al-mithaq), i.e., he undertook it and committed himself to it despite the weakness of his constitution and the feebleness of his strength. This is either an expression for his accepting it according to the requirement of his innate readiness (fitri), or for verbal acceptance on the Day of Covenant. The specification of man by mention, although the jinn are also responsible and likewise the angels, peace be upon them, and although there is no hardship for them in it since there is nothing in it contrary to their natures, is because the address is with him. God the Exalted's words ﴿Indeed, he was very unjust and very ignorant﴾ are a parenthetical statement (i'tiraD wasat) between the bearing and its purpose, to indicate from the outset that he would not fulfill what he undertook. The emphasis (al-ta'kid) is for the case of doubt. That is, he was excessive in injustice and exaggerated in ignorance, according to the majority of his individuals, who did not act according to the requirement of their sound innate nature or their prior acceptance, as distinct from those other than them who did not alter the nature of God the Exalted, "an alteration" (tabdilan). For the truth of a judgment about a species it suffices that it exists in some of its individuals, let alone in most of them. To the first group (al-fariq al-awwal) reference is made by God the Exalted's words:

[p. 97]

﴿So that God may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the idolatrous men and the idolatrous women﴾: that is, man bore it so that God Most High might punish some of his kind who did not observe it and did not respond to it with obedience. The lam here is of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), for punishment, although it was not the purpose of bearing the trust, became, with respect to some of mankind, a result attached to the act, in the way purposes are attached to actions. So it is expressed in the form of purpose. That is, the outcome of man's bearing of it was that God Most High would punish those of his kind who betrayed the trust and wholly departed from obedience. He has alluded to the second group, and by His words, glorified is He, ﴿and God will turn in forgiveness toward the believing men and the believing women﴾: that is, the outcome of his bearing it was that God Most High would turn in mercy toward those of his kind, meaning He would accept their repentance, since they did not wholly cast off the yoke of obedience from their necks, and since they made amends for the lapses that came from them, lapses which a human being rarely escapes by virtue of his nature, and made up for them through repentance, turning back to God, and turning. The Name of Majesty is mentioned first to magnify the matter and to cultivate awe, and the explicit mention in place of the pronoun is used a second time to highlight the greater concern for the matter of the believers, so as to give each of the two stations, that of threat and that of promise, its due. Thus did some eminent scholars say in explaining the verse.

Beyond this there are other views. It has been said that the trust is obedience, because it is inseparable from existence, just as the trust is inseparable from its discharge. The statement is then a confirmation of the gracious promise indicated by His words, ﴿And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has indeed achieved a great success﴾, by making the magnifying of the matter of obedience a means to that end: whoever upholds the rights of so great a matter and observes it is worthy of attaining the good of both abodes.

It has been objected that making the trust, which by its nature comes from Him, Exalted is He, a designation for obedience, which is one of the acts of the obligated and follows from the obligation, is far from being a [proper] approximation. It has also been objected that interpreting the statement as a confirmation in the manner described is contradicted by the description of man as wrongdoing and ignorant at the outset, and by the explanation of bearing [the trust] through the punishment of one group and the turning in mercy toward another group in the second place. It may be said that the intent of that speaker is that the trust is obedience insofar as He, Mighty and Majestic, commanded it, and that His words, ﴿Indeed, he was﴾ and so on, mean that he was so if he did not observe its right. So reflect.

Ibn Jarir and others related from Ibn 'Abbas that the trust is the obligations (fara'id), and something similar was related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. This is other than what was mentioned first, on the basis that the legal obligations are meant in the verbal-noun sense rather than the sense of the passive participle. It has also been said that it is prayer. It is related from 'Ali, may God ennoble his face, that whenever the time of prayer came, his noble face would turn yellow and its color would change. He was asked about this and said: "The time of a trust has come upon me, which God Most High offered to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, and they refused to bear it and feared it. I have borne it, despite my weakness, so I do not know how I shall discharge it."

Al-Safiri reported that it is the ritual bath from impurity (ghusl min al-janabah). It has also been said that it is prayer, fasting, and the ritual bath from impurity. 'Abd al-Razzaq and 'Abd ibn Humayd related from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The trust is three: prayer, fasting, and the ritual bath from impurity." In a report from al-Suddi and al-Dahhak, it is the common trusts of people and the fulfilment of covenants. It has been said that it is not to deceive a believer or a covenant-partner in anything, small or great. It has been said that it is the word of monotheism, for it is the greatest foundation of the legal obligations.

It has been said that it is the limbs and the faculties. Ibn Abi al-Dunya in al-Wara' and al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: "The first thing God Most High created of man was his private part, then He said: 'This is My trust with you, so do not place it except in its right place.' So the private part is a trust, the hearing is a trust, and the sight is a trust."

It is not hidden that interpreting the trust in the verse as the limbs is something one should not heed, and even if the report mentioned is sound, it does not indicate it. Similar to it, and far weaker than it, is the view that it is the letters of the alphabet, which is hardly said except by the children of the schools. The nearest of the mentioned views to acceptance is that it is the obligations, meaning acts of commission and omission. Singling out some of them for mention in the two reports, if they are sound, does not indicate that it is the trust in the verse and nothing else, for a general term is often singled out for mention for a particular reason.

Abu Hayyan said: "The apparent meaning is that it is everything one is entrusted with, of commands and prohibitions, and matters of religion and worldly life, and this meaning encompasses all that has preceded." There are other views, which will come, God willing.

The sayings of those who hold that it is the obligations have differed concerning what follows. It has been said that the speech contains an elision of a word in construction (mudaf), the meaning being: "Indeed We offered the trust to the people of the heavens etc." This is related from al-Jubba'i, and it is nothing. It has been said that the speech is on its apparent meaning, and so are the offering and the refusal. That is because He, Mighty and Majestic, created for the heavens, the earth, and the mountains understanding and discernment, so they were given the choice regarding bearing it, and they refused. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn al-Anbari related from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "It has reached me that when God created the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, He said: 'I shall impose an obligation, and create a Garden and a Fire, and reward for whoever obeys Me and punishment for whoever disobeys Me.' The heavens said: 'You created me, so I was subjected to the sun, the moon, the stars, the clouds, and the wind. I am subjected as You created me. I do not bear an obligation, nor do I seek reward or punishment.' The earth and the mountains said something similar." From what has been mentioned it is known that the refusal was not disobedience, for there was no obligation there, only choice. As for their having regarded themselves as too lowly to be the locus of the trust, that does not remove from them disobedience by refusal if there had been an obligation to bear it.

It has been said: there is no elision, and the speech is in the mode of figurative representation, as you have heard at the outset.

Many have held that the meaning of bearing it is undertaking the duty of upholding it. The one referred to by "man" is Adam, peace be upon him. It has been disputed whether his bearing of it came after it was offered to him or without it. It has been said that it came after the offering. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related: "God Most High offered the trust to the lowest heaven, and it refused. Then to the one next to it, and it refused, until He had finished with them. Then to the earths, then to the mountains. Then He offered it to Adam, peace be upon him, and he said: 'Yes,' between my ear and my shoulder," and so on in the report.

It has been said: without it. Ibn al-Jawzi said: "When God, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam, peace be upon him, and breathed the spirit into him, the trust was represented to him as a rock. Then He said to the heavens: 'Bear this.' They refused and said: 'My God, I have no strength for it.' Glorified is He said to the earth: 'Bear it.' It said: 'I have no strength for it.' He, Exalted is He, said to the mountains: 'Bear it.' They said: 'I have no strength for it.' Then Adam, peace be upon him, came and moved it with his hand and said: 'If You will, I shall bear it.' So he bore it until it reached his hips, then he placed it upon his shoulder. When he bent to put it down, he was called from the side of Might: 'O Adam, stay where you are, do not put it down. This trust has remained upon your neck and the necks of your offspring until the Day of Resurrection, and for you is reward in bearing it and punishment in abandoning it.'" This indicates that the bearing is in its literal sense, and that the offering to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains took place in Adam's hearing, peace be upon him. Ibn al-Anbari went to this.

Some reports indicate that the offering to them took place before Adam, peace be upon him, was created. Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid, who said: "When God Most High created the heavens and the earth, He offered them the trust, and they did not accept it. When He created Adam, peace be upon him, He offered it to him, and he said: 'My Lord, and what is it?' Glorified is He said: 'It is that if you do good, I shall reward you, and if you do evil, I shall punish you.' He said: 'Then I have borne it, my Lord.' Between his bearing it and his being brought out [of Paradise] was only the length of time between noon and afternoon prayer."

I think you will prefer from these views that the offering, on the assumption that it came after the granting of understanding and discernment, took place in Adam's hearing, peace be upon him, and that after he heard their refusal, zeal moved him to bear it. Perhaps this will lead you to choose the view that he bore the trust without its being offered to him, as is the apparent meaning of the verse, and by this his being described as he is described is confirmed. But I do not think you would affirm the soundness of the report of the trust being represented as a rock. If you affirm the soundness of meanings being represented in the forms of bodies, as came in the hadith of the slaughter of Death and others, then so be it. I do not incline to the view that the one referred to by "man" is Adam, peace be upon him, even though he is the first of the species and the origin of its chain, because of His words, ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾, for it is far from fitting to describe the chosen one of God, Mighty and Majestic, by the explicit text ﴿Indeed God chose Adam﴾ [Al 'Imran: 33] with excessive wrongdoing and ignorance. That the meaning is "he was a wrongdoer and ignorant" according to the claim of the angels, peace be upon them, is a cold view. Interpreting it as "he was a wrongdoer to himself, in that he bore upon his weakness what powerful bodies could not bear, ignorant to the extent of what he entered into or to the consequence of what he undertook" does not remove the distance. Nor do I find it admirable that the meaning is "it was of his nature, if left to himself, to be such," as it has been said:

Wrongdoing is among the dispositions of souls; if you find one of chastity, it is for a cause that prevents him from wronging.

This is only so on the view that the reference is to the species. Diverting the speech into the mode of istikhdam (a double-meaning usage), like their saying regarding "I have a dirham, and half of it," is far-fetched both in wording and meaning.

It has been said that the trust means absolute submission, comprising the natural and the voluntary. Its offering means its solicitation, which includes seeking an act from one who chooses and desiring its occurrence from another. Its bearing means betraying it and refusing to discharge it. From this comes their saying: "the bearer of the trust" and "its bearer," for one who does not discharge it, so that his responsibility is cleared. And they recited:

If you do not cease discharging a trust, and bearing another, the deposits will expel you.

The Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 33, verse 73 (part 2 of 3):

Then "refusal" (ibā') means abstaining from betrayal and carrying out what is intended. The meaning is that these bodies (ajrām), despite their greatness and strength, refused to betray Our trust and complied with what We commanded them, in accordance with His saying, ﴿We came willingly﴾ [Fussilat: 11]. "Man betrayed it, for he did not do what We commanded him. Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant." Its remoteness is not hidden, and we have not found in the transmitted reports anything that supports it. Yes, the common people say, "The earth does not betray a trust," so much so that it has become customary in our lands that when they want to bury a dead person somewhere and it is not easy for them, they place him in a grave and say, at the time of placing him, addressing the earth: "This is a trust with you for so many months or so many years," and they throw the dust over him and depart. When they dig up the grave before the period has passed, they find him just as they placed him, nothing about him changed, so they take him out and bury him wherever they wish. If he remains until the period they specified has passed, they find him changed. This is a matter whose transmission has reached us by mass transmission (tawātur), and it is something reason finds unlikely. To something similar went Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj, except that he said: "The offering of the trust is the placing of the signs of divine unity in created things." Abu Hayyan transmitted this from him and mentioned the line of verse cited just above, but he criticized it by saying that the carrying in it is not a clear text about betrayal. It was also said that the trust means reason or moral responsibility (taklīf), and that its being offered to them means considering it in relation to their readiness, and their refusal means their natural refusal, which is their lack of fitness and readiness for it, and man's carrying it means his capacity and readiness for it. His being "a wrongdoer, ignorant" is because of the predominance in him of the irascible faculty (al-quwwa al-ghaḍabiyya), which calls to wrongdoing, and the appetitive faculty (al-shahwiyya), which calls to ignorance of the consequences of affairs. It was said that on this interpretation, His saying ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾ connects with what precedes it as its cause, in terms of reason's bearing it, in the sense of depositing it in him, for the sake of reforming the two faculties in him, which need the authority of reason that rules over them. So it is as if it were said: "We charged him with that because of the faculties in him that need to be subdued and controlled." Likewise, if moral responsibility is meant, for most of the purpose of it is to balance those faculties and break their force. From here it was said that this is closer to verification (taḥqīq). It was also said that the trust is His manifestations (tajalliyāt), glorified and exalted, through His Most Beautiful Names and His Exalted Attributes, and its offering to them and their refusal, and man's carrying it, are as mentioned just above.

His saying, ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾, is an explanation of the carrying, pointing to the strength of his readiness. His saying, glorified is He, ﴿that He may punish﴾, is an explanation of the offering, in the sense that "We offered this so that Our majestic and beautiful manifestations might appear," and this is indicated by the statement of the scholar al-Ṭībī, may God have mercy on him: "Indeed God created creation so that they would be loci of manifestation (maẓāhir) of His Most Beautiful Names and His Exalted Attributes. The bearer of the meaning of greatness and magnificence is the heavens, the earth and the mountains, insofar as they are incapable of bearing the rest of the attributes, for they lack the readiness to receive them. For this reason they refused to carry it and feared it. Man carried it because of the strength of his readiness and capacity, since he is a wrongdoer, ignorant. Thus he was singled out from among all created beings to receive the manifestation of the Subduer (al-qahhāriyya), the Accepter of Repentance (al-tawwābiyya) and forgiveness, and he shared with them in receiving the manifestation of mercy, and he has the largest share of it because of the strength of his readiness and capacity." This is a Sufi path, as is not hidden.

I choose that the trust is everything that is entrusted and whose preservation and safekeeping is required, and it has many instances varying in degree of excellence. Its being offered to those bodies was in the manner of giving them the choice regarding bearing it, not as an obligation, and they were addressed in that and understood the address. God, the Mighty and Majestic, is able to create in every atom of the existents life and knowledge, just as He, glorified is He, created them in those possessing minds. Indeed, the philosophers went so far as to affirm the existence of souls for the spheres and voluntary motion for the celestial orbs. Some even said something similar about the stars, and affirmed voluntary motion for them and denied compulsions (al-qawāsir, external forces) there. It was also said that the intended "man" is the genus, and that His saying, ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾, is in the position of an explanation for the carrying.

Describing the genus with the two forms of intensive emphasis (ṣīghatay al-mubālagha) is due to the large number of individuals characterized by wrongdoing and ignorance from among it, even if these two were not in them in the manner of intensive emphasis. Indeed, no individual is free of being characterized by some wrongdoing and some ignorance. And it is not required, in describing the genus with the intensive form, that that attribute be realized in the individuals, all or some of them, in the manner of intensive emphasis. Yes, if that is realized, it is an additional good, as in what we are discussing, for most individuals of man are in extreme wrongdoing and utmost ignorance. Perhaps what is meant by "wrongdoer, ignorant" is one whose nature is wrongdoing and ignorance, and His saying, ﴿that He may punish﴾, etc., is connected to ﴿We offered﴾, in the sense that it is an explanation of it.

In the speech there is an iltifāt (shift of grammatical person) that is not hidden. The mention of punishment is first because it is more fitting to the two attributes of wrongdoing and ignorance. It was also said: because it is a necessary requirement of the trust that its betrayer is held liable, and it is not a requirement of it that its keeper is rewarded. And the pairing of punishment with repentance, rather than with reward or mercy, is to indicate that among the believing men and women there are those from whom what would merit punishment proceeds, and yet they are not punished. This implies that not every wrongdoing and ignorance is punished, and in this there is bringing joy to the believers and grief to their opposites, which is what it is. Also, that is more in keeping with the apparent sense of His saying, ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾. It was said that reward was not taken into account because it is known from His saying, glorified is He, ﴿And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has indeed achieved a great attainment﴾, so the expression used here points to the fact that this is purely by grace. This is as you see. It was also said that the other is because the concluding clause (tadhyīl) is responsible for conveying their mercy and reward.

The author of al-Lawami' reports that al-Ḥasan read "and He turns" (wa-yatūb) in the nominative, as a new sentence, ﴿and God is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾, meaning: intensively in forgiveness and mercy, in that He turned to the believing men and women and forgave them their lapses and rewarded them with the great attainment for their acts of obedience. We ask God, the Exalted, to turn to us, forgive us and reward us with the great attainment. Indeed, He, may His majesty be great and His bounty be universal, is Forgiving and Merciful.

* * *

Among the allusive (ishārī) interpretations in verses of this noble surah is His saying, ﴿O Prophet, fear God﴾, etc. In it is an indication of the great status of piety (taqwā), and likewise the status of every command and prohibition connected to it, upon him be peace and blessings. In it is also an indication that it is not befitting to love the enemies of God, the Mighty and Majestic, since He forbade obeying them, and these two are like mutually implicating things.

﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾: because its position in the body is the position of the ruler in the kingdom, and wisdom requires the unity of the ruler. And in the report: "If two caliphs are pledged allegiance, kill one of them."

It was also said: that is so that its unity may indicate the unity of God, glorified is He, in existence, in the human body, which is the microcosm (al-ʿālam al-aṣghar), in which the macrocosm (al-ʿālam al-akbar) is contained. It should be known that the heart has, according to them, as Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī said, two usages. The first is its usage for the cone-shaped (ṣanawbarī) piece of flesh known to the elite and the common people. The second is its usage for the reality that combines the divine attributes and affairs and the cosmic, spiritual properties and states, and nature. It arises from the social configuration lying between the divine and cosmic attributes and realities, and what these two principles contain of necessary morals and attributes, and what is generated between them after discipline and purification. The manifestation of this is like the appearance of blackness between gall-nut, vitriol and water. This is the heart about which the Truth spoke through the tongue of His Prophet (ﷺ) in His saying, glorified is He: "My earth and My heaven did not contain Me, but the heart of My believing servant, pious, pure and tranquil, contained Me." It is the locus of the Truth's gaze, the platform of His manifestation, the descent-place of His command, and the station of His condescension. The cone-shaped flesh is too base in its form to be the locus of His secret, great and exalted, let alone to contain Him, glorified is He, or to be the highest aim and level of His gaze. They claimed that calling that cone-shaped thing "heart" is metaphorical, by way of naming the attribute by the name of the bearer, and the bearer by the name of what is borne.

﴿Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihār your mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾: in it is that realities do not change, and that in natural kinship there are properties that do not exist in causal kinship. Where are wives from mothers, and adopted sons from sons? Mothers are roots, and wives are not so; sons are branches, and adopted sons are not so. From here it was said: "The child is the secret of his father." Al-Shams al-Fanārī cited this as a ḥadīth in his Miṣbāḥ al-Uns (Lamp of Intimacy) in the form of a definite statement, without attribution or chain, and it is not authenticated according to the scholars of hadith. It is an allusion to the attributes, morals and perfections that the child acquires by transmission from his father, not through turning the heart toward the presence of the divine unseen and the world of meanings. For through that, the child may acquire attributes and morals contrary to the state of his father. From this the secret of ﴿He brings the living out of the dead﴾ [al-An'am: 95; Yunus: 31; al-Rum: 19] becomes apparent.

﴿If you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients﴾: in it is an indication that religion has a kind of fatherhood, and for this reason inheritance may occur through it.

﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾: because he, peace and blessings be upon him, loves for them more than they love for themselves, and leads them on the path that brings them to eternal life.

﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant﴾: that is, in pre-eternity, when they were fixed entities, or on the day of covenant, when they acquired a kind of determination.

﴿That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness﴾: a question of honor, not of reproach. And truthfulness, as they said, is that there be no admixture in your states, no defect in your deeds, and no doubt in your belief. Among its signs are the existence of sincerity without regard for the created, the purification of states without the intrusion of self-admiration, the soundness of speech free of equivocations, distance from deception among people, and perpetual disavowal of power and strength, indeed departing from metaphorical existence out of longing for real existence.

﴿O you who believe, remember God's blessing upon you when hosts came upon you﴾, etc. Some applied what the verses contain of the story of the confederates to what is within the souls, and what they say is not hidden. Among the strange things I have seen is that Shaykh Muḥyī al-Dīn, may God sanctify his secret, divided the saints into categories, and made among them a category called the Yathribites (al-yathribiyyūn). He said: "They are a people among the saints who have no fixed station, as other saints do." He made the saying of the hypocrites, ﴿O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you﴾, an allusion to this. And how many strange sayings are there of this Shaykh, may God forgive him.

﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of God you have a good example for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day and remembers God much﴾: because he, peace and blessings be upon him, is the most perfect of creation absolutely, and the most favored of people by the radiance of the lights of his character. Upon him are those who hope in God, the Exalted, and the Last Day, and who remember Him, may He be mighty and majestic, much, for the polish of their hearts and the strength of their readiness to receive the radiance of lights and the appearance of effects.

﴿Among the believers are men﴾: that is, complete men. As for the statement of some, that they are "those who dispose of existents with the disposal of males over females," it is an ugly statement, from which the hearts of those who follow the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-ṣāliḥ) recoil, as they do from many statements of the Sufis.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 33, verse 73 (part 3 of 3):

﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a graceful release.﴾ etc. In it is an indication that love of this world and its adornment may be a cause of separation from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and of distance from his noble presence, and that love of him, upon him be prayers and peace, is a cause of great reward.

﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality...﴾ etc. In it is an indication that the ugliness of sins and the beauty of acts of obedience vary according to the persons concerned, and likewise they vary according to places and times.

﴿And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair.﴾ This is an indication of the station of submission, and that it is what befits the believers. This ruling is continuous upon the community until the Day of Resurrection, so it is not fitting for anyone who has received a matter from Allah, mighty and majestic, or from His Messenger (ﷺ) to choose for himself other than it, since that implies an accusation against Allah the Exalted and His Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace. And perhaps the indication in the verses that follow is apparent to whoever has even slight attentiveness.

However, they have prolonged discussion concerning the trust (amanah) mentioned in the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust...﴾ the verse. So let us mention some of that, and we say: Shaykh Muhyi al-Din, may his secret be sanctified, said in (Bulghat al-Ghawwas): The Trust that was offered to the heavens and the earth, and they declined to bear it, is the capacity to know Allah the Exalted. No receptivity was found in the heavens and the earth for what man accepted through this formal composition, for he is the fruit of the cosmos. He sees himself in the cosmos and sees his Lord, glorified is He, through the cosmos, which is himself insofar as he is the whole cosmos. Therefore he was able to contain what the cosmos could not contain, and for this reason He, glorified is He, distinguished him with capacity, when He informed that His heavens and His earth could not contain Him, while the heart of the believer among the human species did contain Him. End of quotation.

It seems he meant by his containing the Real, glorified is He, that he is a comprehensive locus of manifestation for the Names and Attributes, in a manner that does not contradict the transcendence of the Real, majestic is His majesty. This is close to what we mentioned in the commentary and said that it is a Sufi path, as is not hidden.

Another said: It is an expression for the Divine effusion without intermediary, and its bearing is specific to man, because his relation to created beings is like the relation of the heart to the person. The cosmos is a person, and its heart is man. Just as the heart carries the spirit without intermediary and it flows from it through the veins, arteries and the like to the rest of the body, so man carries the Divine effusion without intermediary, and it flows from him to the outer and inner aspects of the cosmos through his outer and inner aspects of the works of body and spirit. Thus the outer and inner of the cosmos are inhabited by the outer and inner of man, and this is the secret of the caliphate.

The meaning of his being "wrongdoing" (zalum) is that he wrongs himself, in that he prepared himself to bear a great matter. And his being "ignorant" (jahul) means that he is ignorant of it, in that he did not know its reality and did not grasp from it anything except the animal form characterized by bestial attributes of eating, drinking and procreation. These two attributes, with regard to those who bear the Trust and fulfil its right, insofar as they became a cause for bearing the Trust, are attributes of praise, and with regard to the treacherous, they are attributes of blame. A thing may be blame with regard to one person and praise with regard to another. And Allah the Exalted is the Guide to the straight path, and from Him is sought help in understanding His Mighty and Majestic speech.
